name: Google Security Command Center findings
description: Security Command Center findings delivered to Splunk as Pub/Sub notification messages: one event per finding update, wrapping the finding, the Google Cloud resource it is about and the notification config that sent it.
source: Security Command Center v1 API protos (Finding, Resource, NotificationMessage); Splunk Add-on for Google Cloud Platform source types reference; two captured Pub/Sub notifications.

feed.label: Google Security Command Center findings
feed.description: Security Command Center finding notifications, delivered one per Pub/Sub message: the finding, the resource it is about, and the notification config that sent it.

envelope_publish_time.label: Pub/Sub publish time
envelope_publish_time.description: The Pub/Sub message's own publish timestamp, epoch seconds with a fractional part; the sourcetype's time_field per the sample capture.

gcp_project_id_ta.label: GCP project id (TA field)
gcp_project_id_ta.description: A project id the add-on scopes the event to. Named in the observed column set for this sourcetype; not a literal top-level key in either read fixture, so its extraction rule was not confirmed.

finding_name.label: Finding name
finding_name.description: The finding's own relative resource name: organizations or folders or projects, then sources, then findings, each with an id.

finding_parent.label: Finding source
finding_parent.description: The relative resource name of the Security Command Center source (the detector or integration) that wrote the finding.

finding_resource_name.label: Finding resource name
finding_resource_name.description: The full resource name of the Google Cloud (or other) resource the finding is about; a customer- or partner-defined string when the resource is not on Google Cloud.

finding_state.label: Finding state
finding_state.description: Whether the security issue the finding describes is still present (ACTIVE) or has been addressed (INACTIVE).

finding_category.label: Finding category
finding_category.description: The detector-assigned classification of the finding; the taxonomy group within findings from a given source. Not a fixed enum: literal spelling and casing vary by detector.

finding_external_uri.label: Finding external URI
finding_external_uri.description: A URI, when available, to a page outside Security Command Center with more information about the finding; guaranteed empty or a well-formed URL.

finding_event_time.label: Finding event time
finding_event_time.description: When the detector believes the condition the finding describes first occurred, or was last updated; the accuracy is the detector's.

finding_create_time.label: Finding create time
finding_create_time.description: The time at which the finding was created in Security Command Center.

finding_security_marks_name.label: Security marks resource name
finding_security_marks_name.description: The resource name of the finding's user-managed security marks; observed as the finding's own name with /securityMarks appended.

finding_sp_explanation.label: Explanation (source property)
finding_sp_explanation.description: Free text: why the detector raised this finding. sourceProperties keys are source-defined (finding.proto: managed by the source that writes the finding); this key belongs to the Security Health Analytics storage-bucket detector seen in the read fixtures.

finding_sp_recommendation.label: Recommendation (source property)
finding_sp_recommendation.description: Free text: the fix the detector suggests. sourceProperties keys are source-defined (finding.proto: managed by the source that writes the finding); this key belongs to the Security Health Analytics storage-bucket detector seen in the read fixtures.

finding_sp_exception_instructions.label: Exception instructions (source property)
finding_sp_exception_instructions.description: Free text: how to mark the finding as an accepted exception. sourceProperties keys are source-defined (finding.proto: managed by the source that writes the finding); this key belongs to the Security Health Analytics storage-bucket detector seen in the read fixtures.

finding_sp_has_admin_roles.label: Has admin roles (source property)
finding_sp_has_admin_roles.description: Whether the exposed principal (e.g. allUsers) also holds an admin IAM role on the resource. sourceProperties keys are source-defined (finding.proto: managed by the source that writes the finding); this key belongs to the Security Health Analytics storage-bucket detector seen in the read fixtures.

finding_sp_has_edit_roles.label: Has edit roles (source property)
finding_sp_has_edit_roles.description: Whether the exposed principal also holds an editor IAM role on the resource. sourceProperties keys are source-defined (finding.proto: managed by the source that writes the finding); this key belongs to the Security Health Analytics storage-bucket detector seen in the read fixtures.

finding_sp_project_id.label: Project id (source property)
finding_sp_project_id.description: The GCP project id string the detector recorded for the finding. sourceProperties keys are source-defined (finding.proto: managed by the source that writes the finding); this key belongs to the Security Health Analytics storage-bucket detector seen in the read fixtures.

finding_sp_reactivation_count.label: Reactivation count (source property)
finding_sp_reactivation_count.description: How many times this finding has gone INACTIVE and back to ACTIVE. sourceProperties keys are source-defined (finding.proto: managed by the source that writes the finding); this key belongs to the Security Health Analytics storage-bucket detector seen in the read fixtures.

finding_sp_resource_path.label: Resource path (source property)
finding_sp_resource_path.description: A multivalue ancestor chain for the resource (project, then folders, then organization), most specific first. sourceProperties keys are source-defined (finding.proto: managed by the source that writes the finding); this key belongs to the Security Health Analytics storage-bucket detector seen in the read fixtures.

finding_sp_scanner_name.label: Scanner name (source property)
finding_sp_scanner_name.description: The Security Health Analytics scanner that produced the finding, e.g. STORAGE_SCANNER. sourceProperties keys are source-defined (finding.proto: managed by the source that writes the finding); this key belongs to the Security Health Analytics storage-bucket detector seen in the read fixtures.

finding_sp_severity_level.label: Severity level (source property)
finding_sp_severity_level.description: The detector's own severity label, title case (e.g. High); not the Finding API's severity enum. sourceProperties keys are source-defined (finding.proto: managed by the source that writes the finding); this key belongs to the Security Health Analytics storage-bucket detector seen in the read fixtures.

notification_config_name.label: Notification config name
notification_config_name.description: The resource name of the notification config that generated this notification.

resource_name.label: Resource name
resource_name.description: The full resource name of the Google Cloud resource tied to this notification.

resource_parent.label: Resource parent
resource_parent.description: The full resource name of the resource's parent.

resource_parent_display_name.label: Resource parent display name
resource_parent_display_name.description: The human-readable name of the resource's parent.

resource_project.label: Resource's project
resource_project.description: The full resource name of the project the resource belongs to.

resource_project_display_name.label: Resource project id
resource_project_display_name.description: Named project_display_name in the proto, but its own field comment calls it the project id; read the value, not the field name.

google:gcp:security:alerts.description: Splunk Add-on for Google Cloud Platform's sourcetype for Security Command Center finding notifications pulled over Pub/Sub; one JSON object per message with publish_time, data (the NotificationMessage) and, when present, attributes.
google:gcp:security:alerts.note: The add-on's Source types reference (https://splunk.github.io/splunk-add-on-for-google-cloud-platform/Sourcetypes/, read 2026-09-19) lists this sourcetype's CIM data models as None. Nested fields are dotted (data.finding.category); sourceProperties keys are detector-defined and vary by finding source.

clock_mismatch.text: Three timestamps ride on one event (the Pub/Sub publish_time, finding.eventTime, finding.createTime) and were observed to disagree by days in the one full fixture read. Pick the clock the question needs; do not assume a fixed lag between them.

project_id_lookalikes.text: Up to four fields can carry a GCP project identifier (a_project_id, sourceProperties.ProjectId, resource.project, resource.projectDisplayName) at different levels and in different shapes (full resource name vs bare id). Only sourceProperties.ProjectId and resource.projectDisplayName were confirmed equal, and only in one fixture.

resource_name_mismatch.text: finding.resourceName and resource.name are not the same key read twice: in the read fixture finding.resourceName names the bucket the finding is about while resource.name names the project. Do not treat them as interchangeable.

severity_lookalikes.text: Three severity-shaped fields exist and are not the same thing: sourceProperties.SeverityLevel (detector-written, title case, e.g. High), a top-level severity column named only in the observed-column extraction, and the Finding API's own severity enum (CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW), which appears in neither read fixture.

source_properties_open.text: sourceProperties is a source-defined map; the Finding proto documents only the container, not its keys. The keys read here (Explanation, Recommendation, ScannerName, ...) belong to a Security Health Analytics storage finding; a finding from another detector carries different keys.

cim_unconfirmed.text: The add-on's own Source types page lists this sourcetype's CIM data models as None. The alert-shaped columns (app, dest, dest_type, description, id, severity, signature, signature_id, src_type, subject, type, vendor_account, body) are in the observed column set but their search-time definition was not readable: treat their meaning as unconfirmed, not as a documented CIM Alerts binding.
